subject: car seatbelt
title: What If You Never Wore a Seatbelt?

scenes.text: What if you never wore a seatbelt? The crash itself isn't what hits you.
When a car slams into something, it stops in a split second. You don't. You keep going at full speed.
Until you hit the steering wheel, the windshield, or the people in front of you.
In fatal crashes, about 30 percent of unbelted people were thrown out of the car. Belted: 1 percent.
An unbelted passenger in the back even raises the belted driver's risk of dying by 137 percent.
A belt cuts your risk of dying in a car by 45 percent. Yet nearly half the people killed in crashes weren't wearing one.

description:
What if you never wore a seatbelt? In a crash the car stops, but unbelted occupants keep moving at the same speed until they hit what is in front of them (IIHS).
NHTSA found only 1% of belted occupants in fatal crashes were fully ejected, versus 30% of unbelted ones. Belts cut the risk of death by 45% in cars and 60% in SUVs, vans and pickups, and an unbelted rear passenger raises a belted driver's risk of dying by 137%. Nearly half of people killed in crashes were not belted.
